selection_reasoning: These two tasks form a coherent multi-hop dependency chain. First, the agent must mine polished granite stairs blocks to obtain building materials. Then, using those mined blocks (and potentially other available materials), the agent must build a bridge across a gap or water feature. This creates a natural resource-gathering → construction pipeline. Mining is a fundamental Minecraft action that doesn't require deep domain knowledge, and building a bridge is an observable, verifiable construction task. The dependency is logical: you need materials before you can build a structure.

edges.reason: Building the bridge requires polished granite stair blocks obtained by mining them from the scene

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining polished granite stairs with a pickaxe drops the stair item into the player's inventory. The player starts with 0 polished_granite_stairs and must mine at least 4 from the row of 7 available blocks (enough to span the 4-block-wide water channel for the subsequent bridge task). inventory_has is the preferred rule for mine tasks since the mined drop ends up in inventory.

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind='block') because building a bridge means placing solid blocks over the water channel. The box covers the entire water region (x: -5 to 5, y: -1 to 1, z: 2 to 9) with generous ±2 padding around the actual water zone (x: -3 to 3, y: -1 to 0, z: 4 to 7) to allow creative bridge placement at any position or height. Initially there are zero polished_granite_stairs blocks in this region (only water and stone), so the rule starts unsatisfied. Requiring min_count=4 ensures a full span across the 4-block-wide water gap.

scene_description: A flat grass platform with a row of 7 polished granite stairs blocks near the player spawn. Beyond the stairs is a 4-block-wide water channel (z=4 to z=7) with oak fence posts marking the corners where a bridge should be built. A grass platform exists on the far side (z=8+). The player has a diamond pickaxe to mine the stairs, then must place the mined blocks across the water to build a bridge.
task_text: Mine the polished granite stairs blocks using the diamond pickaxe, then use the mined blocks to build a bridge across the water channel.
design_notes: Player spawns at ~0 ~0 ~-1 facing the row of 7 polished granite stairs at z=2. Water channel spans z=4 to z=7 (4 blocks wide), x=-3 to x=3 (7 blocks across). Far side grass at z=8-10. Oak fence posts at corners mark the bridge zone. Mining 7 stairs yields enough material (only need ~4-7 blocks to bridge across). Diamond pickaxe provided for efficient mining. The scene is compact (~20 block radius) and tasks are sequential: mine first, then build.
